entry_points.text: Detector exposes open, sequential read, write, reposition and release; report emits one entry per record and writes accept one directive under mutex consuming length on success.
Boot option accepts only on and off; early init skips when default-off or errored, else builds caches and registers static regions; late init publishes control and starts scanning or cleanup.
Boot configuration enables resizing once, toggles debug via keyword and emits aggregate plus per-region diagnostics during initialization.
Name query returns start and length with found status under mutex; top-level early free discards unused maps, resets counters, clears scratch mode and accounts freed pages.

exports.text: Early ranges add with node or defaults, remove, add physical, mark hotplug or mirror, and set or clear nomap, noinit, kernel and scratch flags in init.
Enumeration provides forward and reverse subtraction over two collections and page-frame walk over memory with node and attribute filters and terminal encodings.
Boot allocation offers physical range, strict and best-effort node raw, huge-page with fallback and scratch avoidance, and a mandatory wrapper halting boot on failure.
Accounting and membership report reserved sizes with huge or kernel filtering, free-page estimate, and tests for reserved, memory, mapped and full-interval coverage.
Boot to buddy handover frees maximal aligned blocks, marks reserved descriptors, drops unused map gaps, and gates via deferred init and tag clearing with tail queueing.
List LRU inserts and removes with node and cgroup inference, reports occupancy, isolates or moves entries, and walks one shard or a whole node via root then indexed groups.
Version-one helpers remove groups from excess trees, commit charges, fix swap-in accounting and uncharge in batches.
Early setup exposes deferred init, single-page init, full early release and managed-counter reset.

hazards.text: Interval conversion saturates at maximum, stops periodic work before applying and restarts only on nonzero; duplicate cleanup scheduling relies on shared mutex for safety.
Teardown tolerates null node state; dead shards use most-negative sentinel, occupancy transfer warns on negative sources and dying groups avoid new allocations.
Mirror marking is inert without core support; sentinel doubles as reverse-start, over-budget limits must not truncate, scratch retry depends on direction and zero-start needs max order.
Append trusts callers for capacity, so unchecked use overflows the eight-entry table.
Swap-in expects cache membership with lock held and must drop duplicate swap charge promptly under combined accounting to avoid prolonged double counting.

invariants.text: Report facility shares one table and four callbacks across readers; address dumps probe three domains with invalid-argument on miss or bad number.
Disabled cleanup walks registry without global locking, deletes all entries with periodic yielding.
Registry links only aware instances under mutex; unaware bypass the list and no-cgroup builds expose empty operations with matching signatures.
Ownership is null when accounting is off; slab uses pinned per-object extension, others use folio association, private-id lookup needs read protection and folio pins retry.
Enumeration skips only memory extents on node or attribute mismatch, yields gap-clipped overlaps, packs indexes, rounds page frames and signals exhaustion with sentinels.
Limits derive cutoff by consuming extents in order, keep maximal when budget exceeds total, isolate and truncate on cap, round trims inward and support limit get or set.
Unaccepted memory has active queueing and inert variants; deferred init gates boot freeing via per-node threshold in one build and always-ready in the other.
Deferred helper skips early-ready frames and sets grouping, reserved prep labels nodes with restart and noinit skip, scratch and contiguous globals bracket handover, release unreserves and poisons.
Named reservations append without bounds enforcement, lookup skips empty slots, retrieval caches tolerantly, revival checks compat, lengths, alignment and size with inert variant.
Migration control reads zero and accepts only zero or reports unimplemented by build; threshold comparison yields negative, zero or positive ordering.

locks.text: Leak detector combines per-entry interrupt-preserving spin protection, a global scan mutex for control and lifecycle, and read-side sections for registry walks.
Registry mutex guards aware-instance list walks; reparenting orders source before destination shard locks with nesting and marks source dead before index erasure.
Shard, excess-tree and unaccepted-queue updates use spinlocks with interrupt save; out-of-memory uses a dedicated lock and charge paths mask interrupts for per-cpu safety.
Reservation mutex covers the whole lookup, mutation and debug display sequence for name search, release and listing.

state_machines.text: Clear recolors reported unreferenced entries to grey and resets leak flag; directives gate on enabled except clear; async disable stops scanning then reclaims or retains by leak presence.
Instance setup records shrinker or sentinel, forces unawareness when accounting is off, builds shards and index; teardown unregisters and frees; reparenting migrates queues and defers release.
Discard frees only grown region tables via slab or early paths with page-aligned sizing and clears the memory indirection to block further use.
Forward cursor starts zeroed and ends all-ones; reverse starts all-ones then walks down; huge allocation searches, widens node, narrows on scratch overlap and reserves or fails.
Reserved preparation labels nodes and marks nomap with restart on growth, then inits non-noinit ranges; early low-memory release clears hotplug, prepares and frees outside fixed nodes.
Preserve unwinds prefix on failure; handover build preserves and registers with staged unwind; release returns pages and frees slot; boot params validate then revive or allocate.
Group teardown walks every node and detaches existing per-node accounting from its excess tree.

structs.text: Boot state holds memory, reserved and physical sets with 128, 128 and 4 slots, names, direction, limits, resize and debug flags, mirror state and slab markers.
Region carries base, length, flags and node; collection holds count, array, size and name; zone has lock, unaccepted list and counters; shard has list, lock and occupancy with node totals.
Named reservation entry holds short name, start and length; table is a fixed array of eight with live count under mutex and names limited to sixteen bytes.
Excess forest uses per-node trees with lock; events bind group and channel; ids pack sixteen-bit halves; counters order usage, limit, peak, failures; loops 100 and 2, batches 128 and 1024.
Control uses nine prefixes, 64 staging with 63 usable, kmemleak 0644; flags cover hotplug, mirror, nomap, driver, scratch, noinit, kernel, huge with wildcards.
